explainer.what: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server lets external AI tools — like Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any MCP client — talk to Specrails directly. They can browse your projects, read specs, and (if you allow it) launch work, all through one secure local connection.
explainer.how: Turn it on below, then copy the client config into your AI tool. Specrails only listens on your own machine — nothing is exposed to the internet.
explainer.grants: By default tools get read-only access. Use the permission tiers to grant more, one capability at a time.

enable.enableFailed: Could not enable the MCP server: {{message}}
enable.disableFailed: Could not disable the MCP server: {{message}}

tiers.heading: Permission tiers
tiers.description: Each tier a client may use. Read is always on; the rest are off until you grant them.
tiers.readHelp: Browse projects, specs, and analytics. Always allowed.
tiers.writeHelp: Create and edit specs and tickets.
tiers.aiSpawnHelp: Launch AI rails and jobs that run the CLI.
tiers.destructiveHelp: Delete specs, tickets, and other project data.

config.heading: Client config
config.description: Paste this into your MCP client. It contains no secret — the token is copied separately.

token.heading: Access token
token.description: Your client authenticates with this token. Treat it like a password.
token.regenerateConfirm: Regenerate the access token? Any client using the old token will stop working until you update its config.
